cluster.notes: Clustered qualitatively across body-tier titles + summaries. Top clusters with >=2 body sources: Starmer resignation, Greenspan obituary, Colombia runoff result, China rare-earth retaliation, AI data-center backlash, US-Iran Switzerland talks conclude, Europe heatwave, Reflecting Pool, Warsh Fed task forces, Ukraine/Crimea strikes.

notes: Slot 1 (Starmer) qualified for the lead via the mandate escape hatch (mandate_count=2: Bloomberg + Economist) despite World being non-core; a sitting G7 prime minister's resignation is the kind of cross-aisle World story the rule was designed for.

US-Iran Switzerland talks scored raw 7.37 after a 0.5 dedupe penalty (4th consecutive day on the front page); Europe heatwave scored raw 7.80. Both were ranked below slot 5 because the composition floor (3 of 5 in CORE_BEATS) binds — dropping a non-core slot for a core-beat one was required to meet the floor.

AI data-center backlash (raw 2.25) was placed at slot 5 as the strongest available core-beat with at least 2 body-tier sources; the cluster cleared the >=2-body minimum with Axios and CNBC after The Hill and Wired direct fetches were blocked.
Direct WebFetch was blocked by the Anthropic egress proxy for: apnews.com, reuters.com, bloomberg.com, theguardian.com, dw.com, bbc.com.
Curl with a desktop Chrome UA worked for: cbsnews.com, cnbc.com, foxnews.com, aljazeera.com, washingtonexaminer.com, semafor.com, axios.com (after googlenewsdecoder resolution).
Curl was blocked by Cloudflare/PerimeterX bot-walls on thehill.com (px-captcha) and by the egress proxy on bbc.com, apnews.com, reuters.com, theguardian.com, dw.com, bloomberg.com.
googlenewsdecoder (pip-installed at runtime) resolved Google News RSS article shells to canonical destination URLs; this unblocked Axios, Semafor x2, and Washington Examiner across slots 1-5.
Every dossier carried >=2 body-tier sources with body length >=600 chars (slot 1: 4 sources; slot 2: 3; slot 3: 3; slots 4-5: 2 each).
